questions.scenario: A web app has a production slot and a staging slot. The connection string named OrdersDb must always point to the production database in the production slot, even after a swap.
questions.question: What should you do?

options.text: Mark the OrdersDb connection string as a deployment slot setting in both slots
options.why: Correct. Slot settings stay with their slot during a swap.

options.text: Enable auto swap on the staging slot
options.why: Auto swap automates the swap. It does not keep the setting in place.

options.text: Configure traffic routing to send 0 percent of traffic to staging
options.why: Traffic routing controls user traffic, not which settings move during a swap.

options.text: Store the connection string in the web app code
options.why: Values in code move with the code during a swap.

questions.explanation: Mark environment-specific values, such as databases and endpoints, as deployment slot settings.

questions.question: A web app runs on an App Service plan in the Basic tier. You need to create a staging slot. What should you do first?

options.text: Scale up the App Service plan to the Standard tier or higher
options.why: Correct. Deployment slots require Standard, Premium or Isolated tiers.

options.text: Scale out the plan to three instances
options.why: Adding instances does not enable deployment slots.

options.text: Create a second App Service plan
options.why: A slot runs on the same plan as the app.

options.text: Enable Always On
options.why: Always On does not enable deployment slots.

questions.explanation: Standard allows 5 slots per app and Premium v3 allows 20.

questions.question: You plan to swap a staging slot into production. You need to validate the staging slot while it uses the production slot settings, before traffic is switched. What should you use?

options.text: Swap with preview
options.why: Correct. Swap with preview applies the target settings and pauses so you can validate before you complete the swap.

options.text: Auto swap
options.why: Auto swap completes the swap automatically after deployment, without a pause.

options.text: A custom backup
options.why: A backup does not validate a slot with production settings.

options.text: Clone settings from production when creating the slot
options.why: Cloning copies settings once at creation and does not pause a swap.

questions.explanation: After validating, complete the swap or reset it to cancel.

questions.question: Which two items remain with the production slot after you swap a staging slot into production? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: The custom domain names bound to production
options.why: Correct. Custom domain names are not swapped.

options.text: The scale settings of production
options.why: Correct. Scale settings are not swapped.

options.text: The application code deployed to staging
options.why: The code is swapped and becomes production.

options.text: App settings that are not marked as deployment slot settings
options.why: Non-sticky app settings move with the swap.

questions.explanation: Custom domains, non-public certificates and TLS settings, scale settings, IP restrictions and managed identities stay with their slot.

questions.scenario: You need to send 10 percent of production users to a staging slot to test a new feature. Users must stay on the same slot for the rest of their session.
questions.question: What should you configure?

options.text: Traffic routing with 10 percent assigned to the staging slot
options.why: Correct. Traffic routing sends a percentage of users to a slot, and a cookie keeps them on that slot.

options.text: An autoscale rule on the App Service plan
options.why: Autoscale changes the instance count. It does not split traffic between slots.

options.text: Two access restriction rules with different priorities
options.why: Access restrictions allow or deny traffic. They do not route a percentage to a slot.

options.text: Swap with preview
options.why: Swap with preview validates a swap. It does not split production traffic.

questions.explanation: The x-ms-routing-name cookie keeps each user on the slot they were routed to.
